patch.value: Run the test suite against TypeScript sources behind an uncheatable coverage gate

Coverage was unmeasured here. Tests imported the compiled output from dist/, so the only numbers obtainable pointed at generated JavaScript offsets rather than lines an author edits, and no threshold was wired into any gate.

Tests now import the TypeScript sources directly. Node strips types without a flag since 22.18.0, which is the floor this package already declares in engines, so this needs no new tooling. Enabling rewriteRelativeImportExtensions lets a source file import its siblings as ./x.ts while tsc still emits ./x.js into dist, leaving the published artifact's module graph unchanged.

Two source files used TypeScript parameter properties (constructor(public readonly ...)), which Node's strip-only mode cannot handle. These were refactored to explicit field declarations so the sources run directly under Node without a compiler.

The server entrypoint (src/server.ts) cannot be imported without side effects — it starts an HTTP server and requires a database. A test was added that spawns it as a subprocess without DATABASE_URL, asserting it exits non-zero, which makes the entrypoint contribute coverage through Node's subprocess V8 coverage aggregation.

The gate (scripts/coverage-gate.ts) enforces per-dimension thresholds AND reconciles the reported file list against a walk of the source tree. That second check is the reason it is a script rather than a bare flag: Node omits files that never load from its coverage report entirely instead of reporting them at zero.

value.text: Negative control: created src/__probe.ts exporting one unused function, ran node scripts/coverage-gate.ts — exit code 1, and the gate named src/__probe.ts as never loaded. Deleted the probe and re-ran the gate — exit code 0. The source-presence reconciliation is confirmed not vacuous.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Node omits files that never load from its coverage report entirely, rather than reporting them at zero. A bare --test-coverage-lines flag is therefore satisfiable by narrowing what the suite imports. The coverage-gate.ts script reconciles the reported file list against a walk of the source tree to turn that silent omission into a failure naming the missing files. Additionally, Node's strip-only mode does not support TypeScript parameter properties (constructor(public readonly x: string)) — these must be refactored to explicit field declarations. Subprocess V8 coverage IS aggregated by the test runner, so spawning an entrypoint as a subprocess contributes its coverage to the report.

patch.value: Implemented coverage gate per fleet recipe. Baseline measured at 49.54/80.65/44.83 (line/branch/function) across 26 source files. Thresholds pinned at floor: 49/80/44.
Local gates pass (check, coverage, audit, pack:dry-run, changelog:check). CI legs on Node 22 and 26 are unobserved until the PR runs.

Coverage gate rolled out: tests now import TypeScript sources directly, scripts/coverage-gate.ts enforces per-dimension thresholds plus source-presence reconciliation. All 169 tests pass, negative control confirmed exit 1 with probe and exit 0 without. Gates (npm run check, npm run release:check) pass locally. Two source files refactored to remove parameter properties for Node strip-only compatibility. Server entrypoint exercised via subprocess test.
